> >Yes. P:Solomon cannot be called if there are no contested cards.

> And what about a Dramatic Upheaval if we are only two players left in

They switch places, of course. For all practical purposes, this means no
effect, but there is certainly no ambiguity about the situation.

Similarly, I assume that, for all practical purposes, one could call a
Kindred Restructure that names a "new" seating order which, for all
practical purposes, is virtually identical to the old.

-- John Whelan

legb...@my-deja.com wrote:

> LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote:
> > P:Solomon cannot be called if there are no contested cards.
> >
> Is this an extension of a meta-rule which says something like: if
> there is no target for card x, then card x cannnot be played? i

No, it's just the application of that rule (ruling). No extension
needed there.

If a card/effect chooses/names/selects something, the it cannot
be played if there is no valid "something" to be chosen.

> ask because of calling Kindred Segregation or peace treaty when
> there are no allies or guns in play, calling a parity shift when
> you have the most pool, and stuff like that. Just curious about
> the legalities of some card-cycling ploys!

Peace Treaty can be played with no guns in play, so long as there
are weapons of some form in play to be burned. :-)
Kindred Segregation cannot be played if there are no allies in play
to be burned.
Partity Shift cannot be played if there is no Methuselah with more
pool than you.
